children: Foreign airlines are investing in the Indian market with new products and services amid increasing competition with Air India and IndiGo.
These changes come with the recovery in outbound travel which had seen a dip in the June-end quarter because of the West Asia crisis.

While Malaysia Airlines and Swiss will be deploying their Airbus A330neo and Airbus A350 to Delhi and Mumbai respectively in winter season, SAS Airlines from Denmark will operate its higher capacity Airbus A350 on Mumbai route in summer schedule.
“Our focus for summer 2027 is on adding capacity where we see clear demand,” Erik Westman, Executive Vice President and Chief Revenue Officer of SAS, said on Tuesday.

Malaysia Airlines, which operates 80 weekly flights to ten Indian cities, continues to see growth in leisure, corporate and visiting friends and relatives travel segments. At present Malaysia Airlines flies the A330neo aircraft that features business class suites with privacy doors and new entertainment system to destinations like Auckland, Bali and various cities in Australia. From mid-January it will introduce the aircraft on one of its two Delhi flights offering a consistent product experience to passengers travelling between India-Australia and New Zealand.

Swiss, which is part of the Lufthansa Group, is also upping its ante. On October 27 it launched its maiden service between Zurich and Bengaluru and from December 15 it will deploy an Airbus A350 aircraft on Mumbai route offering passengers greater comfort. The airline said the A350 aircraft has an entirely redesigned business class cabin offering passengers more comfort and privacy. The aircraft will also cut down travel time between Mumbai and Zurich by around 25 minutes to 8.10 hours due to its more powerful engines.

“India is a market with enormous potential and Bengaluru is one of Asia’s leading technology and innovation hubs. We are making a targeted investment in the growth of our long-haul network while also strengthening Switzerland’s international connectivity,” Swiss Chief Executive Officer Jens Fehlinger said while launching the Bengaluru flight.

Air India has begun deploying its new and retrofitted Boeing 787 aircraft on various routes in Asia and Europe as well as Toronto in Canada. Over the next two months it will deploy the new products on Bengaluru-London and Mumbai-Tokyo routes.
On its part IndiGo has also stepped up its focus on IndiGoStretch, its business class product.

“I think we’ve probably been a bit shy about promoting the product in the premium market. I think it’s an excellent product. More and more people are getting to know about it. People are very encouraged when they experience it,” IndiGo Chief Executive Officer Willie Walsh said in the post-second-quarter conference call.

According to Union Tourism Ministry data, while the first two months of CY 2026 saw a growth in outbound travel, March and April saw over 20 per cent decline in departures of Indian nationals. The data includes purpose of travel such as leisure, business, education, pilgrimage and captures details of diaspora members returning home. Traffic volume has since then recovered with a negative growth of 2-4 per cent between June and August.
In the post-second-quarter conference call, Thomas Cook India said it is seeing 30 per cent growth in forward bookings for outbound leisure trips, signalling a positive momentum.

“Traditional markets like Thailand, Singapore, Dubai and western Europe are seeing growth. New markets like Armenia, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan are getting popular with tourists because of their proximity and less expensive flight options,” said Rajiv Mehra, General Secretary of Federation of Associations in Indian Tourism & Hospitality.

title: Foreign carriers upgrade services as competition heats up in Indian skies
